newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends lower on refined product weakness.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends lower on refined product weakness.

text.p: NYMEX crude prices ended off Monday after the restart of gasoline making units and lower gas oil futures in London conspired to push refined product prices lower, traders said.
"The market was generally weak, and on top of that you had some cat crackers coming back on line," said a trader.
December gasoline ended down 1.15 cents a gallon at 65.77 cents. December heat settled off 0.76 cent a gallon at 71.85 cents while December crude ended down 29 cents at $23.88 a barrel.
"There was little else to push crude except for products," said a dealer in Oklahoma.
Sun Co Inc, confirming its forecast from last week, said it restarted early Monday the 85,000 barrel per day catalytic cracking unit at its Marcus Hook, Pennsylvania refinery following maintenance.

The company also said its 80,000 barrel per day crude distillation unit will be returning to service later Monday after its scheduled maintenance. Meanwhile, conventional unleaded gasoline in the U.S. Gulf and New York Harbor cash markets had weakened by 0.75 cent in mid-afternoon.
Heating oil lost ground despite forecasts of temperatures cooling starting Tuesday to below normal in the U.S. Northeast, which uses more heating oil than any place else in the world.
Traders said weakness in gas oil futures on London's IPE halted an attempt by heating oil to retrace losses.

Gas oil, the European equivalent of heating oil, was weaker on news barges set to deliver a record amount of gas oil were backed up in Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp, northwest Europe's oil and refining hub, dealers said.
Traders said there was concern that some November gas oil may not make the delivery window and would be held in storage for December delivery, increasing supplies for the month.
December gas oil fell $2.00 a tonne to $218.75 on the IPE.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
